## Development Standards (MANDATORY)

<!-- DO NOT EDIT this file directly. It is maintained by fhc sync and will be overwritten.
     Source: templates/partials/standards-checklist.md in fh-commons -->

**All items below are MANDATORY. No exceptions.**

### File & Code Structure

- [ ] Max ~500 lines per file; split into packages as needed
- [ ] Modular, config-driven scripts, menus, modals, and forms
- [ ] DRY enforced strictly (no exceptions without prior discussion)
- [ ] No hardcoded values (paths, URLs, ports, file lists from config)
- [ ] Fail fast (no fallbacks, no silent error swallowing)
- [ ] Complies with `ARCHITECTURAL_STANDARDS.md`

### Helper Usage (in priority order)

- [ ] 1. fh-commons helpers checked first (`docs/python-functions-reference.md`)
- [ ] 2. Existing app helpers checked second
- [ ] 3. New helper created only if truly needed (consider adding to fh-commons)

## Testing Policy — E2E + Lint Only

**This is a one-user homelab project. We do NOT write unit tests.**

Unit tests are a waste of time in this context: they test implementation details, duplicate coverage that e2e tests already provide, and routinely pass while real behavior breaks. Do not write them. Do not plan for them. Do not add them to "Tests to Write" sections. If you see `tests/unit/` in an existing plan, strike it and replace with `tests/e2e/`.

### What IS allowed

| Type | Location | When |
|------|----------|------|
| **Lint** (`ruff check`) | changed `.py` files only | Every change that touches Python. Always. |
| **E2E — CLI** | `tests/e2e/test_<area>.py` | Any change that affects a `` command, a pipeline stage, or a cross-module flow |
| **E2E — Browser** (Playwright) | `tests/browser/test_<area>.py` | Webapp changes only. Skip if the project is not a webapp |

Everything else is **BANNED**.

### What IS banned — no exceptions

| Banned | Why |
|--------|-----|
| New files under `tests/unit/` | Policy: no unit tests |
| `tests/unit/test_*.py` references in issue plans | Policy: no unit tests |
| Testing internal functions in isolation | Test via the CLI / pipeline / browser instead |
| Adding unit tests to "improve coverage" | Coverage as a goal is banned — behavior verification is the goal |

<!-- DO NOT EDIT this file directly. It is maintained by fhc sync and will be overwritten.
     Source: templates/partials/mock-ban.md in fh-commons -->

**Mocks are BANNED. No exceptions.**

| Banned Pattern | Why |
|----------------|-----|
| `unittest.mock` / `@patch` / `MagicMock` | Replaces real behavior with fake behavior |
| `pytest-mock` / `mocker.patch()` | Same — just a different API |
| `Mock()` / `MagicMock()` | Fake objects that hide real failures |
| Dry-run mode as test substitute | Tests must run real commands |

**The pre-commit hook BLOCKS commits containing mock patterns.**

Tests must use:
- Real `subprocess.run()` for CLI commands
- Real filesystem operations (use `tmp_path`)
- Real database/network calls (or `pytest.skip` if genuinely unavailable)

### E2E Test Requirements (when you write one)

An e2e test must:

- [ ] Invoke the **real CLI** via `subprocess.run` (or drive the **real browser** via Playwright for webapp tests)
- [ ] Use **real filesystem** operations (`tmp_path` is fine for isolation)
- [ ] Use **real database** / **real network** calls, or `pytest.skip` if the resource is genuinely unavailable
- [ ] Verify **observable outcomes** (exit code, output, file contents, DB rows, page state) — not internal function calls
- [ ] Cover the direct feature + at least one regression/adjacent path

### Test Gate — what must pass before a branch is pushed

- [ ] `python -m ruff check $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- '*.py')` exits clean
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_<relevant>.py` passes (or an explicit, commented `pytest.skip` documents why a prerequisite is unavailable)
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/browser/test_<relevant>.py` passes (webapp projects only)
- [ ] ` verify --check-artifact` passes for the current HEAD, or
      ` verify` is run and produces a current passing verify artifact
- [ ] `grep -rn "tests/unit/" <your-diff>` returns empty — no new unit-test files added

No current passing verify artifact means the branch is not done, ready for
review, deployable, or finishable.

That last line is load-bearing. If you catch yourself writing a unit test, stop and rewrite it as an e2e test or delete it entirely.
